headline: SRE IV / DevOps / Automation & AI Engineer
_titles_note: 2026-09-13 per Vic: trajectory set to AI/Agentic specialist for the next-20-years direction. Added agentic/AI-forward IC and leadership titles above rather than replacing the existing SRE/platform/DevOps base, that base is the real current strength and the credible path INTO AI/agentic roles, not a competing track. Vic explicitly deferred whether to drop/deprioritize the plain ops titles (devops engineer, cloud engineer, automation engineer) until seeing this diff, see session summary for the removal-candidate list.

search_titles._note: Single source of truth for what actually gets SENT to search APIs (Remotive/Adzuna's free-text query params). Separate from target_titles above, which is used for downstream scoring/filtering only, a job can score well on target_titles but never even enter the pool if nothing here ever searched for it. Set 2026-08-27 per Vic: previously radar.py hardcoded 3-4 infra-only phrases duplicated 4x across US/DE/NL/ES Adzuna calls, so CTO/CIO/Head of AI/Senior AI Engineer/SRE Manager/Senior SRE Lead/Senior AI Lead were NEVER searched for anywhere, no matter how well profile.json's own scoring would have ranked them if they'd shown up. Kept deliberately as literal multi-word phrases (not the shorter fragments in target_titles) since these get sent verbatim to external free-text search params.

comp_targets._note: CHANGED 2026-09-14 per Vic, explicit direct instruction: hard floor of 80,000 USD/year applies uniformly across every tier already targeted, Senior through CTO/Head of AI/Head of Platform. This replaces the previous ~28%-blended-tax GROSS proxy (90k net / 0.72), that approach was always flagged as a guess with no real per-country tax model behind it (see the standing 'taxes handled differently by country' rule, US/EU/Spain-Beckham-Law all vary wildly and blending them into one percentage was false precision). Simpler and more honest now: 80,000 is treated as a plain disclosed-GROSS floor, matching exactly what job boards (Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby/Adzuna/RemoteOK) actually report. No radar.py code change needed, meets_comp_floor() already applies min_comp_monthly_usd uniformly to every matched job regardless of seniority tier, and is_senior_or_leadership() already gates the pool to Senior+ IC and Manager-through-CTO/CIO titles, exactly the 'Senior roles to CTO/Head of AI/Head of Platform' range Vic specified.

_differentiator_note: Added 2026-09-14 per Vic ('tech sectors where my experience can make the difference'). Scored the same as strong_skills (2pts) rather than good_skills (1pt) in radar.py's score(), since these represent real hands-on background (PCI-DSS/CDE ownership on FlexPOS, IoT/OT device+peripheral governance via the TCA framework, PingFederate/OAuth/SSO ownership), not just familiarity. A posting mentioning these alongside SRE/DevOps/AI titles signals a role where Vic's specific cross-domain background is a genuine edge over a typical candidate, not just another qualified applicant. See session summary for the full sector breakdown (payments/fintech, industrial IoT/mining-adjacent, agentic AI platforms, identity/security, observability tooling vendors).

track_c_europe._neutral_note: Added 2026-09-23 per Vic (geopolitical hedge: EU/EEA states with a formal policy of military non-alignment, i.e. not NATO members, kept distinct from a frontline-exposure read). Ireland, Austria, Malta, and Cyprus are EU members with constitutional or long-standing neutrality; Switzerland is EEA-adjacent (EFTA/Schengen, not EU) but the same neutrality profile, kept in this list for the same reason. Malta and Cyprus added to the country list above for the first time this session, they were previously absent from track_c_europe entirely. This is a tagging list for downstream shortlisting/filtering only, not a radar.py scoring change, non-neutral countries already in track_c_europe (Finland/Estonia border Russia directly, Poland/the Baltics are frontline NATO states) are left in place, unchanged, this only adds an additional lower-exposure option, it does not remove or deprioritize existing ones.
track_c_europe._note: Widened 2026-09-13 per Vic (career-radar scope review): added France/Austria/Belgium/Italy/Poland/Czech Republic/Estonia/Luxembourg. Widened again 2026-09-23 (Malta/Cyprus, neutral-country hedge). Same caveat as the earlier Spain widen, adding a country here only helps once a company on the watchlist (radar/companies.json) or Adzuna actually has an opening there, country breadth alone is necessary but not sufficient.

track_e_latam._note: Added 2026-09-13 per Vic: roles based in or explicitly open to Chile/LatAm, no relocation needed. Deliberately no visa_terms key, sponsorship/relocation language doesn't apply to a home-region role the way it does for Track C/D/F, so no visa badge is computed for this track (see tracks_of() in radar.py).

track_d_us_sponsor._note: Deliberately no 2-letter state codes (CA/NY/TX/WA), those false-hit constantly inside ordinary words. Location field is short and structured, full state/city names are enough. preferred_regions set 2026-08-26 per Vic: Texas (named explicitly) + New England + Upper Midwest + Mountain West, chosen for lower violent crime / higher standard of living over a 30-year horizon. Hard filter: a job pinned to a non-preferred state is excluded even if otherwise remote-tagged. A job with no pinned state at all (generic 'Remote, US') passes if genuinely remote, since the employer isn't dictating a location, that's compatible with living in Texas. Renamed from us_indicators/preferred_states to the generic country_indicators/preferred_regions 2026-09-13, that generalization is now unused by any other track (Track F/Canada was tried and dropped per Vic 2026-09-14, not interested), kept generic anyway since it cost nothing and the next country-based track can reuse it without a rename.

direct_portals._note: Added 2026-09-13 per Vic (career-radar scope widen, Big Tech + some AI-native companies). radar.py can only automate Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby (public opt-in ATS JSON feeds) plus the Adzuna aggregator, see radar/radar.py's src_greenhouse/src_lever/src_ashby. Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Apple all run custom in-house career sites with no public JSON feed, they cannot be added to radar/companies.json the same way Stripe or Datadog can, doing so would just silently fail (same HTTPError pattern already documented there for Spain scaleups on Workday). Rather than pretend these are automated, they're listed here as direct search-portal links, same honest pattern as track_a_walmart_markets above: surfaced in the daily digest for a manual check, not scored/graded like Tracks B-F.

direct_portals_chile._note: Added 2026-09-14 per Vic (mining sector + Chile sectors above 7,500 USD/month). Real research via web-retriever, not guessed: mining is a credible high-pay sector for senior automation/AI/OT/digital-transformation talent in Chile (autonomous trucks, digital twins, predictive maintenance are real active investment areas), but NONE of the majors run a Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby public feed. BHP and Teck are confirmed on SAP SuccessFactors (verified from page script references), Codelco/SQM/Antofagasta Minerals/Anglo American/Albemarle/Glencore's exact platforms are unverified/custom, none have a documented public JSON board API the way Stripe or Datadog do. Same for banking (Banco de Chile, Santander Chile, BCI, Itau), energy (Enel Chile, AES Andes), and telecom (Entel, Movistar, Claro), all plausible for Director/Head-of/CTO-level comp above the threshold, none automatable. Only URLs actually confirmed reachable during research are listed below, same honest standard as direct_portals above, no guessed/unverified links included. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: unlike Tracks B-F, nothing here is scored, graded, or comp-filtered, radar.py cannot evaluate these against the 80k/year (or any) floor since there's no JSON feed to read salary from, this is a pure manual-check list surfaced in the daily digest.
direct_portals_chile.target_comp_context: Vic's ask 2026-09-14: sectors clearing 7,500 USD/month (~90,000 USD/year) in Chile specifically. Real finding: this is NOT typical for an ordinary local senior IC hire in Chile, even in mining, it's realistic mainly at Director/Head-of/CTO/regional-technology-leadership level, or for expatriate/regional packages with allowances layered on top of base salary. This is a DIFFERENT number from the global 80,000 USD/year floor set for profile.json's comp_targets (that one applies to remote/global-band roles across Tracks B-F), not a change to it, flagging the distinction rather than silently conflating the two.

_high_confidence_note: Added 2026-09-23 per Vic's literal ask: 'companies where I can score 75 or more as a candidate'. This is radar's own cheap keyword-based match pct (grade_of() in radar.py, 0-99 range from raw skill/title keyword hits), NOT the same instrument as career-assessment's deep per-requirement 0-100 ATS fit score (that one needs a human/agent JD-fit pass against MASTER_CAREER_FACTS.md, can't run at radar's every-job-every-day automated scale). Treat radar's 75%+ list as a first-pass shortlist filter: postings worth taking to the real ATS evaluator for a full fit-score and probability read, not a substitute for it. Checked against live data the day this was added: current top score across the whole watchlist was only 70% (1 job), so 75%+ is a real, currently-unmet bar today, not a rubber stamp.
